description.sr:
Napiši funkciju `countWords(text)` koja vraća objekat sa brojem pojavljivanja svake reči.

Reči se razdvajaju razmacima, a velika i mala slova se ne razlikuju.

Primeri:
- `countWords('a b a')` → `{ a: 2, b: 1 }`
- `countWords('Hello hello')` → `{ hello: 2 }`
- `countWords('')` → `{}`
description.en:
Write a function `countWords(text)` that returns an object with the number of occurrences of each word.

Words are separated by spaces, and case does not matter.

Examples:
- `countWords('a b a')` → `{ a: 2, b: 1 }`
- `countWords('Hello hello')` → `{ hello: 2 }`
- `countWords('')` → `{}`

text.sr:
Deklaracija funkcije `countWords`.

- `function countWords` pravi funkciju sa tim imenom; test je poziva baš tako.
- `(text)` je parametar: string u kome brojimo reči. Kad pozovemo `countWords('a b a')`, unutar funkcije je `text` jednako `'a b a'`.
- `{` otvara telo; zatvara ga `}` u liniji 8.
text.en:
Declaration of the function `countWords`.

- `function countWords` creates a function with that name; the test calls it exactly like this.
- `(text)` is the parameter: the string in which we count words. When we call `countWords('a b a')`, inside the function `text` equals `'a b a'`.
- `{` opens the body; it is closed by `}` on line 8.

text.sr:
Pravimo prazan objekat koji služi kao rečnik: ključ je reč, a vrednost je broj njenih pojavljivanja.

- `const` pravi promenljivu koja se ne može ponovo dodeliti (ne možemo napisati `counts = nešto drugo`).
- `{}` je prazan objekat. Posle punjenja izgledaće npr. `{ a: 2, b: 1 }`.
- Sadržaj objekta se i dalje može menjati (dodajemo ključeve u petlji), jer `const` štiti samo vezu između imena i objekta, ne sadržaj objekta.
- Napredna napomena: običan objekat nasleđuje svojstva, pa je `counts.constructor` funkcija, a ne `undefined`. Za reč `constructor` bi ovaj kod dao pogrešan rezultat. Testovi to ne proveravaju, ali u praksi bi se koristio `Map` ili `Object.create(null)`.
text.en:
We create an empty object that serves as a dictionary: the key is the word, and the value is the number of its occurrences.

- `const` creates a variable that cannot be reassigned (we cannot write `counts = something else`).
- `{}` is an empty object. After filling it will look like `{ a: 2, b: 1 }`.
- The object's contents can still change (we add keys in the loop), because `const` protects only the link between the name and the object, not the object's contents.
- Advanced note: a plain object inherits properties, so `counts.constructor` is a function, not `undefined`. For the word `constructor` this code would give a wrong result. The tests do not check that, but in practice you would use a `Map` or `Object.create(null)`.

text.sr:
Petlja koja prolazi kroz sve reči teksta, jednu po jednu.

- `text.toLowerCase()` pretvara ceo tekst u mala slova, da `Hello` i `hello` budu ista reč (to zadatak traži). Stringovi su nepromenljivi, pa dobijamo novi string, a `text` ostaje isti.
- `.split(/\s+/)` seče string na niz reči. `/\s+/` je regularni izraz (šablon za traženje): `\s` je bilo koji beli znak (razmak, tab, novi red), a `+` znači „jedan ili više uzastopnih“. Zato više razmaka zaredom deluje kao jedan razdelnik i ne prave se prazne reči između.
- `for (const word of ...)` uzima jedan po jedan element tog niza; u `word` je u svakom prolazu trenutna reč.
- `{` otvara telo petlje; zatvara ga `}` u liniji 6.

Za tekst `'Hello hello'`:

```
toLowerCase()  → 'hello hello'
split(/\s+/)   → ['hello', 'hello']
prolaz 1: word = 'hello'
prolaz 2: word = 'hello'
```
text.en:
A loop that goes through all the words of the text, one by one.

- `text.toLowerCase()` converts the whole text to lowercase, so `Hello` and `hello` are the same word (the task requires this). Strings are immutable, so we get a new string and `text` stays the same.
- `.split(/\s+/)` cuts the string into an array of words. `/\s+/` is a regular expression (a search pattern): `\s` is any whitespace character (space, tab, newline), and `+` means “one or more in a row”. So several spaces in a row act as one separator and no empty words are created between them.
- `for (const word of ...)` takes the elements of that array one by one; in `word` there is the current word on each pass.
- `{` opens the loop body; it is closed by `}` on line 6.

For the text `'Hello hello'`:

```
toLowerCase()  → 'hello hello'
split(/\s+/)   → ['hello', 'hello']
pass 1: word = 'hello'
pass 2: word = 'hello'
```

text.sr:
Preskačemo prazne stringove, da se ne broje kao reči.

- `split` ume da vrati prazan string. `''.split(/\s+/)` vraća `['']` (niz sa jednim praznim stringom), a tekst sa razmakom na početku ili kraju, kao `' a b '`, daje prazne elemente na krajevima: `['', 'a', 'b', '']`.
- `!word` je „nije word“. `!` obrće istinitost. Prazan string se u JavaScript-u ponaša kao „neistinit“ (falsy), pa je `!''` jednako `true`.
- `continue` znači: „preskoči ostatak tela petlje i pređi na sledeći element“. Zato se prazan string nikad ne upiše u `counts`.
- Skriveni testovi proveravaju baš ovo (više razmaka, razmaci na krajevima).
text.en:
We skip empty strings so they are not counted as words.

- `split` can return an empty string. `''.split(/\s+/)` returns `['']` (an array with one empty string), and text with a space at the start or end, like `' a b '`, gives empty elements at the ends: `['', 'a', 'b', '']`.
- `!word` is “not word”. `!` flips truthiness. In JavaScript an empty string behaves as “falsy”, so `!''` equals `true`.
- `continue` means: “skip the rest of the loop body and move on to the next element”. That is why an empty string is never written into `counts`.
- The hidden tests check exactly this (several spaces, spaces at the ends).

text.sr:
Povećavamo brojač za trenutnu reč za jedan.

- `counts[word]` čita svojstvo objekta čije je ime u promenljivoj `word`. Uglaste zagrade koristimo jer ime nije fiksno nego se menja. Ako reč još nije viđena, svojstvo ne postoji i vrednost je `undefined`.
- `??` (nullish coalescing) vraća desnu stranu samo ako je leva `null` ili `undefined`. Ovde: ako reč nije viđena, računamo od `0`; ako jeste, koristimo već upisani broj.
- `+ 1` dodaje jedan, a `=` na početku upisuje rezultat nazad u `counts[word]`.
- Zagrade su važne: `counts[word] ?? 0 + 1` bi se pročitalo kao `counts[word] ?? (0 + 1)`, jer `+` ima viši prioritet od `??`. Brojač tada nikad ne bi rastao iznad prve vrednosti.

Tok za `'a b a'`:

```
word = 'a' → counts['a'] je undefined → (undefined ?? 0) + 1 = 1   counts = { a: 1 }
word = 'b' → counts['b'] je undefined → (undefined ?? 0) + 1 = 1   counts = { a: 1, b: 1 }
word = 'a' → counts['a'] je 1         → (1 ?? 0) + 1         = 2   counts = { a: 2, b: 1 }
```
text.en:
We increase the counter for the current word by one.

- `counts[word]` reads the object's property whose name is in the variable `word`. We use square brackets because the name is not fixed but changes. If the word has not been seen yet, the property does not exist and the value is `undefined`.
- `??` (nullish coalescing) returns the right side only if the left is `null` or `undefined`. Here: if the word has not been seen, we count from `0`; if it has, we use the number already stored.
- `+ 1` adds one, and the `=` at the start writes the result back into `counts[word]`.
- The parentheses matter: `counts[word] ?? 0 + 1` would be read as `counts[word] ?? (0 + 1)`, because `+` has higher precedence than `??`. The counter would then never grow beyond its first value.

Flow for `'a b a'`:

```
word = 'a' → counts['a'] is undefined → (undefined ?? 0) + 1 = 1   counts = { a: 1 }
word = 'b' → counts['b'] is undefined → (undefined ?? 0) + 1 = 1   counts = { a: 1, b: 1 }
word = 'a' → counts['a'] is 1         → (1 ?? 0) + 1         = 2   counts = { a: 2, b: 1 }
```

text.sr:
Zatvara telo petlje otvoreno u liniji 3.

- `}` je par za `{`. Svaka otvorena `{` mora da ima svoju `}`; ako jedna fali, JavaScript uopšte ne može da pročita kod (`SyntaxError`).
text.en:
Closes the loop body opened on line 3.

- `}` is the pair of `{`. Every opened `{` must have its `}`; if one is missing, JavaScript cannot read the code at all (`SyntaxError`).

text.sr:
Vraća popunjen rečnik.

- Za prazan tekst petlja nije dodala nijedan ključ (sve su preskočene), pa je rezultat `{}`, što test traži.
- `return` odmah završava funkciju i šalje `counts` pozivaocu.
text.en:
Returns the filled dictionary.

- For empty text the loop added no keys (everything was skipped), so the result is `{}`, which the test requires.
- `return` ends the function immediately and sends `counts` to the caller.

text.sr:
Zatvara telo funkcije otvoreno u liniji 1.

- `}` je par za `{`. Svaka otvorena `{` mora da ima svoju `}`; ako jedna fali, JavaScript uopšte ne može da pročita kod (`SyntaxError`).
text.en:
Closes the function body opened on line 1.

- `}` is the pair of `{`. Every opened `{` must have its `}`; if one is missing, JavaScript cannot read the code at all (`SyntaxError`).

note.sr: Prazne stringove treba preskočiti jer `''.split(/\s+/)` vraća `['']`.
note.en: Empty strings must be skipped because `''.split(/\s+/)` returns `['']`.
